topic: Chat QA database: hook into agent chats, classify my responses against agent questions, store Q&A pairs in Postgres on the VPS
initialPrompt: I wanna build some kinda script app that stores my chats with ai agents. (the questions agents have, and my responses only), and stores that on my vps backend (postgres). I wanna create a database of my answers to questions. And basically how im thinking it will work is that we'll hook into whenever I send an message to an agent in the harness we take that message I sent, and the most recent agent response (the message i am responding to) send both of those messages to an ai model, and have the ai model detect whether or not my question answers the question. If my answer answers the question, and the question is a question it gets added to the database.

qAndA.question: Capture mechanism: a pi extension using the input event (fires the moment I send a message), pulling the last assistant message from the session branch — the same pattern the official qna.ts example uses. Skip non-interactive inputs, mid-stream interrupts, queued follow-ups, and inputs starting with /
Classification is fire-and-forget: it runs in the background and never blocks or delays my message. Failures go to a local log file; no popups.

Storage: reuse the existing appdb on the VPS (postgrest-db, Postgres 17) — new chatqa schema + dedicated role, connected from this machine via PgBouncer at 100.122.184.37:6432 (already ACL-allowed and covered by the daily pg_basebackup). No new containers.

Schema: append-only Q&A pairs — source, session name, model, question text, answer text (verbatim), created_at, plus question/answer hashes with a unique constraint so exact duplicate pairs are skipped.
Classifier verdict is structured JSON: has_question + answers_it. Stored only when both are true.
V1 captures going forward only. Existing session files are local JSONL, so a backfill pass is feasible later.
V1 has no query UI — the DB is browsable via Beekeeper (already set up) and could later be exposed through PostgREST at b0tts.dev/api.

Scope: which agents should this capture? (a) Pi only — built as a pi extension, fastest to v1, source column added so other harnesses can join later. (b) Multiple harnesses (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) — each needs its own hook mechanism, significantly bigger v1. Recommendation: (a) pi only for v1.
qAndA.answer: b, but we will focus on pi for now. but we will work with multiple harnesses.

qAndA.question: Revision of decision #1: capture layer becomes a source-adapter abstraction (each harness = one adapter) with pi as the first adapter; schema is multi-source from day one (source column first-class, per-harness metadata). Pi-only implementation in v1.

Classifier model: which model runs the classification on every message? (a) opencode-go deepseek-v4-flash (your default) — cheapest and fastest, plenty for a yes/no classification. (b) Current session model — costs more when on a pro model. (c) openrouter deepseek-v4-pro — most accurate, most expensive. Recommendation: (a) flash.

Classifier extraction fields: The classifier LLM returns structured JSON with has_question (boolean), answers_it (boolean), extracted_question (clean standalone question snippet), and extracted_answer (clean extracted user answer snippet). In Postgres, we store both the extracted clean q&a pair and the full raw verbatim messages for auditability.

Pre-filtering heuristics: To minimize unnecessary API calls to the classifier model, the capture hook first runs a light regex check on the preceding assistant message (checking for ?, numbered/lettered option lists like (a)/(b), or question keyphrases). If no question pattern is present, it skips calling the classifier.

Context Window for Classification: When the user gives a short or contextual answer (e.g. 'a', 'yes', 'option 2', 'use postgres'), the classifier needs to understand what option or question that refers to. What context scope should we send to the classifier model? (a) Immediate pair + small context window (last 3 messages: previous user turn, preceding assistant turn, current user answer) — allows resolving references like 'option 2' from recent context while staying fast. (b) Strict 1:1 pair only (only preceding assistant turn + current user answer) — minimal tokens, but may miss context if options were presented earlier in the response. Recommendation: (a) small context window (3 messages total).

Non-blocking extension execution & error logging: The Pi extension fires the classification HTTP request asynchronously without awaiting it inside the input event handler. Control returns instantly with 0ms delay to user chat. Classification errors or network timeouts are caught silently and written to ~/.pi/logs/chat-qa.log.

Multi-Question Handling: When an assistant message contains multiple questions (e.g. Q1: database selection, Q2: classifier model) and your input answers both of them in one turn, how should the classifier structure and store the results? (a) Multi-row extraction (Array of Q&A pairs) — Classifier identifies each answered question independently and returns an array of pairs; each pair is inserted as a separate clean row in Postgres. (b) Single composite row — Classifier extracts a single combined summary question and combined answer into 1 DB row per user turn. Recommendation: (a) Multi-row extraction, so individual decisions remain cleanly searchable.
qAndA.answer: no extractor for responses. We wont get response from the agent, we will get the raw source/exact user response. dont make the decider reiterate or summarize, or even rewrite.

qAndA.question: Revision of Decision #11 & #15: No LLM extraction or rewriting for user responses. User responses are captured directly from the raw source event payload as pure verbatim text (0 modification, 0 LLM summarization). The classifier LLM operates purely as a decision gate (has_question: boolean, answers_it: boolean), returning classification flags plus the extracted question string from the assistant message if present.

Assistant Question Storage Format: Since user responses are strictly raw verbatim text, how should the assistant's question be stored in the DB? (a) Extracted question snippet + raw context — Classifier extracts the concise question/options snippet for 'question_text', while the full unedited assistant message is stored in 'raw_assistant_message' for auditing. (b) Full raw assistant message only — Store the entire unedited assistant message directly in 'question_text' with 0 LLM extraction on either side. Recommendation: (a) Extracted snippet for question_text, with raw_assistant_message as backup.
